summary: Apply EPA SWMM, QGIS, and runoff methods to urban drainage challenges. Explore the five-day course outline and plan your training.
lede: Drainage design training helps drainage engineers, urban planners, and operations staff assess runoff and drainage performance. Participants map catchments in QGIS, select rainfall inputs, estimate runoff, and review EPA SWMM network outputs for capacity constraints, surcharge, and flooding. They also compare SuDS and LID options and prioritize practical drainage interventions using methods such as the Rational Method and Manning equation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, plan, operate, or review urban stormwater and drainage assets. It suits intermediate learners with some exposure to drainage, water resources, or infrastructure work.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with urban drainage, civil infrastructure, hydrology, or water resources is recommended. Basic spreadsheet use is helpful; coding is not required. EPA SWMM and QGIS exercises are planned using sample training datasets. A laptop with the course software installed is recommended; both applications are available without a commercial licence.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
